successors.name: Roman Republic
successors.text: the upper Aniene, Tolenus and Himella valleys east of Latium

capitals.name: Carsioli district (upper Turano), the Aequian centre

ledger.x: c. 500 BC: the Aequi 'occupied the upper reaches of the valleys of the Aniene, Tolenus and Himella', east of Latium. No formation date; 500 is a placeholder before the first dated events (their chief centre taken 'about 484 BC', Algidus 458).
484-458 BC: the Aequian wars: 'Their chief center was taken by the Romans about 484 BC'; 'The Battle of Mount Algidus is dated 458 BC'.
458 BC: Algidus; 'Records of fighting become much sparser in the second half of the 5th century BC'.

c. 394 BC: 'Their chief center is said to have been taken by the Romans about 484 BC and again about 90 years later'; in 389 BC 'the Etruscans, Volsci, and Aequi all raised armies' and Camillus defeated the Aequi; a Roman raid on Aequian territory in 388; then silence 'until 304 BC'. The page does not name the centre…
388 BC: the raid; the Aequi 'disappear from the sources until 304 BC'.

304 BC: 'not finally subdued' until 'the closing phase of the Second Samnite War (326 to 304 BC)'; Rome 'punished them in 304 BC, and Livy wrote that "the Aequian name was almost blotted out"'; Alba Fucens founded 303, Carsioli 302-298.
304 BC: conquest; civitas sine suffragio offered (undated).

certainty.note: Three Apennine valleys; the region is the roman-republic dossier's.
